Usage: mcpjam cloud eval [options] [command]
Author and run eval suites in your hosted MCPJam projects
Options:
-h, --help display help for command
Commands:
create [options] Create a runnable eval suite from authored test
cases (does not run it)
list [options] List the eval suites saved in a project
runs [options] List a suite's run history, newest first
revisions [options] List a suite's settings history, newest first
run [options] Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a
versioned suite file and run it. The
upload-and-launch has a 120s deadline overall, not
per request (raise it with the global --timeout
<ms>); --wait-timeout bounds the RUN instead.
status [options] Get the status and summary of an eval run
stage-analytics [options] Read the user-value chain funnel for one run
(--run) or a suite's runs as a trend series
(--suite)
route-facts [options] Read the tool routes a run's trials took — which
paths were used, and which expected tools were
missing or substituted
server-facts [options] Read the server a run was taken against — tool
surface, catalog size, annotation coverage,
tool-metadata signals, and what connect and
discovery observed
description-experiment Propose, start, or read a two-arm tool-description
53:The file is invalid when it is not JSON, when `version`, `apiUrl` or `lock` is missing or has the wrong type, when `version` is
not `1`, when it has any other key, when it cannot be read, when `apiUrl` has credentials, a query or a fragment, or when `apiUrl
` uses plain `http://` to a host other than a loopback address.
70:| The locked MCPJam server (API, CLI login settings) | Allowed |
73:| URLs the locked server returns (model leases, artifact downloads, tunnel relay) | Allowed: your server chose them |
74:| The sign-in provider your server's login settings name | Allowed |
82:When `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY` is set (either case), the CLI process sends its `fetch` requests through the proxy and honor
s `NO_PROXY`: MCPJam's API, model providers and MCP servers over HTTP. `HTTPS_PROXY` covers `https` destinations and `HTTP_PROXY`
covers `http` ones; with only `HTTP_PROXY` set, `https` requests use it too. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` always connect d
irectly, so local MCP servers and the local Inspector keep working. A value without a scheme, such as `proxy.corp.com:8080`, means
`http://`; a value that is not an http(s) URL is ignored with a warning. Two connections do not use the proxy yet: the relay conn
ection of `mcpjam cloud tunnel` and the `mcpjam oauth` debugging proxy.
